title: AI beyond the hype | Wood Mackenzie
gist: Energy Gang podcast episode summary in which AIQ CTO Saravan Penubarthi argues AI creates value in energy only when moved from pilots to daily operations, citing a 2-5% production gain at ADNOC across 148 rigs. The framing is that real-deployment evidence, not ambition, will decide trust as AI nears control of critical assets; the page is a short show-notes blurb with sponsor (ADIPEC) content.

insights.claim: Energy-sector AI vendors argue that AI creates value only when it moves from pilots into day-to-day operations, using tools built around energy-specific problems and tested alongside customers.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Favor energy-AI vendors with production deployments and customer co-development over pilot-stage names.
insights.locator: Saravan argues that AI creates value when it moves from pilots

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's framing is that the energy industry's AI promise is still running ahead of the proof, and that evidence from real deployments will matter more than ambitious claims about eventual capability as AI moves closer to controlling critical assets.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Discount vendor claims lacking repeatable, measurable gains; watch for audited deployment results.
insights.quote: evidence from real deployments will matter more than ambitious claims about what the technology might eventually do
insights.locator: For operators, the test is whether

insights.claim: AIQ's CTO cites a 2 to 5 per cent production improvement for ADNOC from its AI solutions, which are deployed across 148 ADNOC rigs.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: A vendor-reported, unaudited uplift of this size on a large national oil company is the benchmark to test against other operators' AI claims.
insights.locator: Saravan cites a 2 to 5 per cent production improvement

insights.claim: AIQ says its computer-vision systems for safety, security and productivity generate more than a billion camera-based predictions a day.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Indicates scale of industrial computer-vision inference demand in energy operations.
insights.locator: more than a billion camera-based predictions a day

insights.claim: AIQ's product range spans prediction, recommendations and in some cases autonomous action, with examples including RoboWell, which adjusts well controls, plus emissions-monitoring work and expansion into international markets.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Shows AI moving from analytics toward closed-loop control of wells; watch for international customer wins.
insights.locator: He describes a model that spans prediction

insights.claim: AIQ distinguishes assisted AI, where people approve recommendations, from autonomous operations, which it says require extensive testing, fallback mechanisms and clear human oversight.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Safety, fallback and accountability requirements gate the pace of autonomy adoption in critical energy assets.

insights.claim: AIQ is developing Genesis, an AI-native operating system for energy, slated to be unveiled at ADIPEC.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Watch the ADIPEC unveiling (Abu Dhabi, 2-5 November) for product detail and customer commitments.
insights.locator: He says AIQ is developing Genesis

insights.claim: Energy security and resilience have moved to the top of the industry agenda after repeated supply disruptions, which is why AI is being pitched as a way to anticipate equipment failures and respond faster to risk.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Supply-disruption concern supports operator budgets for reliability-oriented AI and predictive maintenance.
insights.locator: Energy security and resilience have moved to the top of the agenda
